Content:
A quadrantal angle is an angle whose terminal side lies on the [MATH: x] or [MATH: y]-axis.
The unit circle below illustrates the quadrantal angles that lie on the range [MATH: [0^\circ, 360^\circ).]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/89d766661fd33e20975b611b0e9d931f]

Content:
We can identify four points on the unit circle above,

Content:
[MATH: (1,0), \quad (0,1), \quad (-1,0), \quad (0,-1),]

Content:
that correspond to the angles

Content:
[MATH: 0^\circ, \quad 90^\circ,\quad 180^\circ, \quad 270^\circ,]

Content:
in degrees, or

Content:
[MATH: 0, \quad \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \quad \pi, \quad \dfrac{3\pi}{2},]

Content:
in radians.

Content:
We can use these points to find cosine and sine of quadrantal angles. First, recall that a point [MATH: (x,y)] on the unit circle is related to the central angle [MATH: \theta] using the following formulas:

Content:
[MATH: x = \cos\theta, \qquad y = \sin\theta]

Content:
For example, if we are asked to find the value of [MATH: \cos(\pi),] then we just look at the [MATH: \color{blue}x]-coordinate of the corresponding point. The point is [MATH: ({\color{blue}{-1}},0),] and therefore, we get

Content:
[MATH: \cos(\pi)={\color{blue}{-1}}.]

items.title: Computing the Tangent or Cotangent of a Quadrantal Angle

sections.normalized_html:
The angle [MATH: \dfrac{3\pi}{2}] is a quadrantal angle. Let's draw out the quadrantal angles on the unit circle.

From the unit circle, we see that the angle [MATH: \dfrac{3\pi}{2}] corresponds to the point [MATH: (0,-1).]

  • Since the cosine of the angle corresponds to the [MATH: x]-coordinate, we have [MATH: \cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) = 0.]

  • Since the sine of the angle corresponds to the [MATH: y]-coordinate, we have [MATH: \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) = -1.]

Therefore, using the fact that [MATH: \tan{\theta} = \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\cos\theta},] we have

[MATH: \tan\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)}{\cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{-1}{0}.]

However, division by zero is undefined. Therefore, [MATH: \tan\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)] is undefined.
